description: hugoh/hk-config//presets/hk-pins is extended through presets/base, so every consumer gets its custom managers (the hugoh/hk-config and jdx/hk pins in *.pkl / mise.toml) and the built-in mise manager is disabled for `hk`. Repos without hk.pkl are unaffected: the managers match nothing. The timezone, soaks (7 days third-party, 1 day hugoh/**), monthly window, vulnerability alerts and automerge presets also come from presets/base.

packageRules.description: config:best-practices pulls in security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm, whose rule lowers npm to 3 days and would override the top-level 7 days.

Own group for minor/patch/pin/digest updates of my packages. A group is one branch with one schedule, so a consumer's hugoh/** schedule override (e.g. daily) needs a group of its own, not the generic ones, which would end up with mixed schedules. Majors stay ungrouped. Must stay below the generic minor/patch rules (their groupName would replace it) and above the hk and first-party core rules below, whose groupName must win.

hk and hk-config move together in one weekly PR: a release of either can change checks and fail CI, and hk-config needs a minimum hk version. Read by custom managers (hk.pkl, mise.toml), which is why the generic rules alone would not pair them across update types. Skipped in the hk-config repo, where hk is part of the project: it stays in the generic groups. Both get the 7-day soak: updates join the branch as each matures, so a shorter hk-config soak could land it without the hk it needs. A consumer overriding the schedule of hugoh/** must exclude hugoh/hk-config, or the group gets mixed schedules.

First-party reusable workflows and composite actions: a bump only reaches consumers once a new tag is cut, so propagate within a day and automerge. Only in the repos that own them. Own groupName so the generic minor/patch groups don't impose their weekend schedule instead of "at any time".

The renovate CLI ships several times a day: own group, Saturday-early window. presets/npm-renovate-debounce holds the same rule for go-tools; here it has to sit below the generic minor/patch rules, which would replace its group and schedule (a rule can't extend a preset that holds packageRules).

Look both biome entries up on npm: the mise manager's github-tags lookup finds nothing for the pin, since the tags are named @biomejs/biome@<version>, while the $schema URL (biome.json, read by customManagers:biomeVersions) already uses npm. Nothing else is special: biome is tooling like the rest, so it joins the generic weekly groups and automerges. The pin and the $schema can land in different PRs (a patch next to a minor, or ungrouped majors); biome only warns on a mismatch until the other one merges.
